<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
Partial stagnation occurs over a set of $n-1$ addition operations, when $0<u_i\leq t$ for some $0 < M \leq n-1$ additions and for some given threshold $0 < t \leq p$. Here $t$ is the maximum number of most significant bits used in each of the $M$ addition operations for which the above conditions hold.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{def:tot-stagn}
  Total stagnation occurs over a set of $n-1$ addition operations, when for any $0 < M \leq n-1$ operations $u_i = 0$ and $\operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(\widehat{s_{i-1}} + x_{i}) \in \{\widehat{s_{i-1}}, x_{i}\}$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
Near-total stagnation occurs over a set of $n-1$ addition operations, when for any $0 < M \leq n-1$ addition operations $\operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(\widehat{s_{i-1}} + x_i) \notin \{\widehat{s_{i-1}}, x_{i}\}$, but $u_i=0$ (the addend with the larger magnitude is changed only by rounding).
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{def:ulp}
  Let $x \in \mathds{F}$ with precision $p$, where $x = \pm 2^{e}m$. The unit in the last place is defined as $\operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}(x) = 2^{-(p-1)} \times 2^e$.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
Given $x_1, \dots, x_n \in \operatorname{\mathbb{F}}$ where $x_i\geq 0$ for $i=1\dots n$ and a recursive sum $\widehat{s_n}=\operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(\widehat{s_{n-1}}+x_n)$ with $\widehat{s_1}=s_1=x_1$, if the sequence $x_2,\dots, x_n$ is decreasing or stays constant, total stagnation of length $1$ to $n-1$ can happen.
  \label{thm:stagn0}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The harmonic series is an example of this scenario.
  This is expressed as $1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + \mathellipsis = \sum_{i=1}^\infty 1/i$.
  In real arithmetic the summation diverges.
  In finite precision, the sum eventually grows to a point where the next addend is absorbed completely \cite{malo13}.
  The addends are decreasing, so total stagnation occurs.
  Another example is as follows. Take $x_1=2^{j}$ for $j \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $x_i<2^{j-p-1}$ for all $i=2,\dots, n$.
  Then $\widehat{s_n}=s_1=x_1$ since $\operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(s_1+x_i)=s_1$ for all $i=2\dots n$.
  The proof is analogous for shorter stagnations with $x_i<2^{j-p-1}$ for some $i=2 \dots n$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
Given $x_1, \dots, x_n \in \operatorname{\mathbb{F}}$ where $x_i\geq 0$ for $i=1\dots n$ and a recursive sum $\widehat{s_n}=\operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(\widehat{s_{n-1}}+x_n)$ with $\widehat{s_1}=s_1=x_1$, if the sequence $x_2,\dots, x_n$ is increasing, total stagnation of length $1$ to $n-1$ can happen.
    \label{thm:stagn1}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Take $x_1=1$, $x_2=2^{p+1}$, $x_3=2^{(2p+2)}$ (thus, $x_i=2^{(i-1)(p+1)}$), then $\operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(x_1+x_2)=x_2$, $\operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(x_2+x_3)=x_3$ and so on, giving stagnation of length $n-1$. Stagnation of of length shorter than $n-1$ can be analogously shown.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
Given a decreasing sequence of positive values $x_1, \mathellipsis, x_n \in \mathds{F}$ where $x_{k-1} > x_{k} > 0$ for $k = 2, \mathellipsis, n$
  and a recursive sum $\widehat{s_1} = x_1, \widehat{s_k} = \operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(\widehat{s_{k-1}} + x_k)$,
  total stagnation cannot occur if $x_k > x_1 / 2$ for all $k$ and $2^{p-1}x_1 < N_\mathrm{max}$ where $p$ is the precision of $\mathds{F}$ and $N_\mathrm{max}$ is the greatest normalised floating-point number.
  \label{thm:decsum-lb}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
At step $k$ we are performing $\widehat{s_{k}} = \operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(\widehat{s_{k-1}} + x_{k})$.
  Absorption will not occur at step $k$ if $x_k > \operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}(s_{k-1})/2$, so we will show that this condition can hold provided the assumptions are held.

  First, we will prove the bound $\widehat{s_k} \leq kx_1$.
  We do this by induction.
  \begin{itemize}
    \item $\widehat{s_1} = x_1$ by definition.
    \item $\widehat{s_2} = \operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(\widehat{s_1} + x_2) \leq \operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(x_1 + x_1) = 2x_1$.
    \item Assume $\widehat{s_k} \leq kx_1$.
    \item Then $\widehat{s_{k+1}} = \operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(\widehat{s_k} + x_{k+1}) \leq \operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(kx_1 + x_1) = (k+1)x_1$, provided $k \leq 2^{p-1}$.
  \end{itemize}
  The greatest $n$ such that $x_k > x_1 / 2$ holds for $k = 1, \mathellipsis, n$ is $n = 2^{p-1}$.
  Let $n$ take this value and consider the sum at step $n$.
  The maximum value of the current addend is $x_n = x_{2^{p-1}} = x_1 / 2 + \operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}(x_1)$.
  Assume that the sequence of addends is decreasing at the smallest possible rate, where each subsequent addend is one $\operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}$ less than the previous, or half an $\operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}$ if the previous term is a power of two.
  The accumulator is bounded by $\widehat{s_{n-1}} \leq (n-1)x_1$, so $\operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}(\widehat{s_{n-1}})/2 \leq \operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}((2^{p-1}-1)x_1)/2 \leq 2^{p-2}\operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}(x_1) \leq x_1 / 2$.
  Therefore $x_n > \operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}(\widehat{s_{n-1}})/2$ holds.
  We have shown that if the given lower bound is satisfied, we will not observe stagnation for any recursive summation of decreasing floating point numbers.

  If the sequence $x_1, \mathellipsis, x_n$ decreases at a greater rate than the assumption, the number of terms $n$ when we reach $x_n = x_1 / 2 + \operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}(x_1)$ is less than $2^{p-1}$.
  We will not be able to hold the condition $x_k > x_1 / 2$ beyond this point, and stagnation may occur.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
Given a decreasing sequence $x_1, \mathellipsis, x_n \in \operatorname{\mathbb{F}}$ where $x_i > x_{i+1} > 0$ for $i = 1, \mathellipsis, n$ and a recursive sum $\widehat{s_1} = x_1$, $\widehat{s_{k+1}} = \operatorname{\mathrm{fl}}(\widehat{s_k} + x_{k+1})$ for $k = 2, \mathellipsis, n-1$,
  total stagnation cannot occur if $x_{k+1} > k \operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}(x_1)/2$ for $k = 2, \mathellipsis, n-1$.
  \label{prp:decsum-nostag}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
At step $k+1$ we are adding $\widehat{s_k}$ and $x_{k+1}$. We have $\operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}(\widehat{s_k})/2 \leq \operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}(kx_1)/2 \leq k \operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}(x_1)/2$ by similar working as in Theorem \ref{thm:decsum-lb}, so we can write the condition for no total stagnation as $x_{k+1} > k \operatorname{\mathrm{ulp}}(x_1)/2$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
